questNarration.text: Hello there, friend. It's been a while, hasn't it?
Hello, Liben. How have you been?
Well, I'd say that I've found the proverbial light at the end of the tunnel at last. After returning from Sumeru previously, I did a quick cargo run to Inazuma.
Since things weren't looking so hot in Sumeru, I decided to try my luck in Fontaine instead.
I was just going to observe the market a little, you know, and if I made my capital back? Well, you wouldn't see me complaining.
I never could have been prepared for how much the locals there loved Inazuman goods.
The goods I had on me and couldn't sell in other countries, such as the Ms. Hina merchandise, actually sold out.
Well, that's wonderful.
So Ms. Hina got to show her quality, eh?
The people of Fontaine love messing about with mechanical devices, and relatively few, by contrast, spend time developing such trinkets as these.
I suppose that's the scarcity principle for you.
Hahaha. Well, if it didn't look like dark clouds were gathering there too, I'd have made a few more trips for sure.
What's going on over there?
Well, things just feel oppressive and dangerous... You know, like a storm is about to break out.
The locals were pretty antsy... Said judgment was soon to come, or something like that.
I'd suggest you refrain from going there lest you get yourself into trouble that you can't easily get out of.
I'll bear that in mind.
You be careful too, Liben.
Well, then our arrangement shall be the same as always.
Can you run me through your background again?
I'm Liben, and once upon a time I sold curios.
I've been doing good business recently.
What kind of business are you talking about?

Ah, it's simple. You see, you just need to find me a few basic everyday items, cooking ingredients and the like, and then you trade them with me for a Box o' Marvels that are stuffed full of all kinds of nice little treasures.
Keep in mind that I've filled these Boxes o' Marvels with the fortune I made in my time as a seller of curios. There's no booby prizes to be found here, and I treat all my customers the same.
Why box them up and turn it into a lucky draw, you ask?
What can I say, people like a gift box. It just makes everyone a little more inclined to get involved.
Can you tell me about your background again?
I'm Liben, and once upon a time, I sold curios.
I've been doing good business recently.
Before that, I ran the Nod-Krai trade route, hoping to make myself a small fortune.
But... I'm still here, so I'm sure you know how that turned out!
What kind of business are you talking about?
Simple. You find me a few basic everyday items, cooking ingredients and the like, and then you trade them with me for a Box o' Marvels, full of all kinds of nice little treasures.
Keep in mind that I've filled these Boxes o' Marvels with the fortune I made in my time as a seller of curios. There's no booby prizes to be found here, and I treat all my customers the same.
Why box them up and turn it into a lucky draw, you ask?
What can I say, people like a gift box. It just makes everyone a little more inclined to get involved.
How do you earn any money like this?
Hmm, fair point. Perhaps I should explore business opportunities in Natlan next time after all, eh?
Or maybe hire a few people for protection and make another trip to Nod-Krai, that might work too...
To be honest, though, I'm getting pretty tired...
Guess I'll take a break before making any more plans!
Hello, friend. It's been a long time.
Liben, I trust you've been well?
Life is full of triumphs and setbacks. I've grown used to it, you know. A small illness is nothing to write home about, and minor losses are just part of the game.
So I suppose you could say I've been well enough, ha!
How about you, friend?
Not bad.
That's marvelous to hear!
Not so good.
...Really?
I am overjoyed today, because I have run into you once again, my friend!
Anything interesting happening lately?
Don't you think I ought to head to Natlan and seek out new business opportunities? Seize the day and strike while the iron's hot?
Hahaha, I don't actually want to go to Natlan this time.
A few days ago, I accidentally fell into a hole and spent the whole night staring at the stars.
That definitely doesn't count as having been "well" lately...
Anyway, I was rescued by a passing adventurer, and didn't even get hungry down there! All's well that ends well, am I right?
Looking up at the stars at night, I couldn't help but wonder... What lies beyond this world?
Uh... Endless distance, and endless worlds.
You think so too, friend?
I was thinking how, what if every single star was actually a sun, and each of those suns had a planet orbiting it that we could visit?
Or what if we could even visit every single star themselves? After all, they just give off light, maybe they aren't even that hot?
The nights there would be quite bright. You couldn't sleep with that much light.
Oh, that's true. Then it would be enough just to go look. Though no one could live there like that, so I guess there wouldn't be any business opportunities.
Trying to trailblaze a new trade route?
Do the nations up in the sky use Mora too? But if those places are lit up all day long, then nobody can live there, right?
Back to the matter at hand, our old deal is still on, right? No changes?
Hey there, friend! It's been a while!
It sure has, Liben!
Hehe, enthusiastic as ever, I see... I wonder, how changed a man am I?
You're the same as ever.
Why, you're getting friendlier!
That's good. I mean, I almost didn't make it back this time.
Did you try your luck in Natlan?
Nope! I heard that things there were tense, so I deliberately avoided it and went to Nod-Krai instead.
Have you been there?
Nope.
What kind of place is that?
No? Well, I guess I can tell you about it then.
Nod-Krai is in the southernmost part of Snezhnaya, where people from all over Teyvat gather. Those not in the know would think that opportunities to get rich are everywhere there.
It's only after you get there that you realize that it's a wild place that plays by its own rules.
Its own rules?
Let me put it this way: Before I even set foot in the city, I was robbed by a group of vagrants — taking advantage of my ignorance about the place.
Courts of law, Knights of Favonius... There's none of that there. Someone just told me to visit the Voynich Guild.
Said the Guild was the strongest force in the area and that they might be able to get me justice.
I was only half-convinced at first, so imagine my surprise when the Guild folks not only hauled all my goods back — they even bought everything off me, too. Totally amazing, right?
I was so happy to see that much Mora, I counted it all up several times!
"I've done it! Woohoo!"
...And why did I almost not make it back, you ask?
Ugh... I don't even wanna talk about it. When I left the city again, I ran into another band of vagrants, who robbed me of every Mora — not a single coin was spared.
They must've already had their eye on you back in the city...
*sigh* That's me, Liben, for you! Only the grandest peaks and deepest troughs of life! Anyway, I'm not going back there — not for a while at least.
So yeah, stay on your toes if you're going to Nod-Krai, and don't let just anyone know that you're holding onto a big bag of Mora.
I'll keep that in mind.
You keep your guard up too, Liben.
So, I trust that our deal's still on, then?
